what_happened: The job "Make the explainer site introduce Athena and fix newcomer findings" ended failed. The producer's final report was sent back with problems still present. Four acceptance criteria were unmet or not reported: (1) the page title, first heading and opening paragraph name Athena and say what it is, that the page is an example of its study capability, and that firstmate is the system studied; (2) a visible next-step section with clickable links to the Athena and firstmate repositories, and claim sources as links to files at the pinned commit; (3) the f2 "Limits of this study" text no longer shows the schema phrase "guard_evaluated_by for nobody"; (4) running `cargo run -p xtask -- site` writes index.html under target/site with the Athena heading and repo links, and does not write inside the work tree. One more criterion bundled commands: `cargo test -p xtask` with new tests, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` must be clean. The event lists no blocker or major findings. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Completion is judged only once, when the producer's final report is checked against the criteria. Nothing makes the producer map each criterion to evidence, or run the gate commands and record their results, before it can report done. This job had a long multi-part list. It mixed content criteria, such as title, links and wording, with command runs listed as acceptance items, so it is unclear who runs the commands and when. Rendered-output criteria need the site to be built and its HTML inspected, and nothing requires that step before reporting. Gaps therefore show up at the end as a failed job. This is the third case in this class in one day.
prevention: Add a code gate on the producer's final report. It must carry a per-criterion evidence table, with the command output or file excerpt for each acceptance criterion. It must also carry recorded results of the declared gate commands (test, clippy, fmt, and the site build). The report is rejected back to the producer immediately if any criterion has no evidence or any gate has no recorded pass. Separate the gate commands from the acceptance criteria in the reading, so the system runs them and does not leave them to the producer to remember.
proposed_request: Make the explainer site introduce Athena and fix the newcomer findings. Outcome: when the site is built with `cargo run -p xtask -- site`, target/site/index.html has Athena in the title and first heading. Its opening paragraph says what Athena is, that the page is an example of what Athena's study capability produces, and that firstmate is the system studied. The page has a visible next-step section with clickable links to the Athena repository and the firstmate repository. Every claim source is a link to its file at the pinned commit, not a bare file:line string. The finding f2 "Limits of this study" text is in plain language and does not show "guard_evaluated_by for nobody". Building the site writes nothing inside the work tree. Before reporting done, give a table that maps each criterion above to evidence, such as the HTML excerpt or test name. Also report the recorded passing results of `cargo test -p xtask` (with new tests for the Athena title, next-step links, source links and link-text escaping), `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`.
